newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks continue on upward path in morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks continue on upward path in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks retained their firm tone in Wednesday morning trade, with investors unwilling to sell even after this week's strong rally.
"Ninety percent of the people I talk to say we are going to have a consolidation, yet we are still up," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading at HG Asia.
"There is not enough selling around. If someone wants to see this index go a little higher and may be test that 12,600 level, I don't see what is going to be in its way," he added.
The Hang Seng index was up 68.70 points at 12,559.40. Turnover was HK$2.26 billion after 50 minutes of trade.
The blue chip index has put on 272 points this week and is drawing close to its all-time high of 12,599.23.
"I think the market will remain quite firm," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
Investors continued to gravitate towards major blue chips on Wednesday, with HSBC Holdings up HK$0.50 to HK$152.00 and Henderson Land up HK$0.25 at HK$70.75.
"The market is liquidity driven increasingly by foreign funds. Foreign funds will normally pick the more liquid blue chips," said Kwong.
"May be now investors will start looking for lagging stocks like individual utility and conglomerate stocks," he added.
Hongkong & China Gas was up HK$0.30 at HK$13.40 but China Light was off HK$0.10 at HK$37.30 and HongKong Telecom fell HK$0.10 to HK$13.95.
Shares in Wheelock & Co rose HK$0.10 to HK$17.95 and Hutchison added HK$0.25 to 54.25.
"One of the reasons it (the market) has been able to sustain itself is because of rotation," said Lesko.

Shares in CEF Concord rose HK$0.08 to HK$1.11. International Tak Cheung Holdings said it was holding preliminary negotiations with CEF which might result in a reorganisation. ITC Holdings was down HK$0.04 at HK$1.89.
Trading in shares of Sun Hung Kai & Co was suspended at the company's request pending an announcement. The stock closed at HK$2.40 on Tuesday.
